review_result: Issues Found: 3 Major core proof defects; 3 Minor range or constant defects

problems.title: False quartic separation in the analytic continuation proof
problems.proved_evidence: Expansion gives left minus right=-51/25 exactly. Zero sum cancels first moment but not third moment.
counterevidence_and_alternative_readings: Lemma8.4 only supplies valid Jensen M|y|^4; does not supply sum|phi|^4 addition.
problems.core_dependency: Lemma2.1 analytic continuation ->Cor2.2 ->Section4 main last-scale representation.
problems.repair_status: Coercive bound A>=(sum|phi|^4+M|y|^4)/17 proved; compact complex-mass domination; cross-multiply before analytic continuation to avoid assumptions about partition-function zeros.
problems.independent_computation: checks/independent_checks_001.json; decisive analytic proof in exact bound report section

independent_verification.assessment: The coefficient-one quartic separation after (2.34), page 30, is false on the actual mean-zero fluctuation space. For n=1 take phi=(2,-1,-1,0,...,0) and y=-1/10. Sum phi=0, sum phi^2=6, sum phi^3=6; the difference sum|phi+y|^4 - sum(|phi|^4+|y|^4) is 4y*6+6y^2*6=-51/25. The pad-zero example lies in Im(Q_N)^perp at every allowed volume >=3 and in the support of the real nondegenerate mean-zero covariance for a>-L^(-2(N-1)). Small positive g cannot repair the deterministic inequality.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Mean-zero cancels the linear term in phi but not sum phi^3. The Jensen bound used later on pages 90â€“91 only gives sum|phi+y|^4 >= M|y|^4 and does not imply coefficient-one separation. Source Lemma 2.1 feeds Corollary 2.2 and the central moment identities; this is a false step in a core derivation, not a demonstration that the moment identities or final scaling laws are false.
independent_verification.repair: Let A=sum|phi+y|^4. Mean-zero Jensen gives M|y|^4<=A; |u-v|^4<=8(|u|^4+|v|^4) gives sum|phi|^4<=16A. Hence A >= (sum|phi|^4+M|y|^4)/17. With g>0 this controls compact-parameter quadratic and linear factors and supplies the missing integrable domination. For continuation one can cross-multiply holomorphic numerator/denominator identities rather than assume the partition function is zero-free throughout the complex half-plane. Repairability does not remove Major calibration for the invalid core derivation.

independent_verification.assessment: The domain (5.28),(5.36) gives a large-field bound proportional to theta_j^3 gtilde_j^(3/4) rho_j^p with p=a-b. At d>=12, (5.27) sets p=d(1-epsilon)/(2(d-4))<3/4; (6.10) instead asserts rho^(3/4) for all d>=4. The proof explicitly infers this from domain membership and uses it for Theorem 3.1 (3.12). For n=1, mass zero and d>=12, set H(t)=t^6 exp(-c t^4), c>kappa, and K_j(phi)=eta gtilde_j^3 rho_j^p H(phi/h_j). For sufficiently small fixed eta and small g this belongs to the stated domain uniformly in j but violates the claimed rate at phi=h_j as j grows.
independent_verification.independent_derivation: This example satisfies the infinite analytic-derivative norm, not merely a finite Taylor norm. Cauchy's estimate on radius-two complex circles bounds the full scaled derivative sum by twice the maximum of |H(t+z)|; for real t, Re(t+z)^4=t^4+O(|t|^3), so c>kappa gives the required regulated decay. At zero, the absolute Taylor sum is r^6 exp(c r^4) with r=ell_j/h_j=C gtilde_j^(1/4) rho_j^(1/4). Thus the two W-norm contributions are bounded by constants times eta gtilde_j^(9/2) rho_j^(p+3/2) and eta gtilde_j^(21/4) rho_j^(p+b). Since b=3(1-epsilon)/2<3/2 and a=p+b, these fit the domain radius C_RG gtilde_j^3 rho_j^a at mass zero. At phi=h_j, division by the proposed bound leaves a nonzero fixed-g factor times rho_j^(p-3/4), diverging because p<3/4 and gtilde_j tends to a positive small limit for d>4.
independent_verification.counterevidence: This disproves the asserted domain implication; it does not claim the specially initialized RG trajectory K_0=0 realizes the counterexample. An additional trajectory estimate could repair the gap, but is not provided by domain membership. Epsilon cannot simply be set to zero: source (9.4),(9.23) use the strict margins to absorb L-dependent constants. With the explicit epsilon=1/(2d-6), the domain decay exponents are 17/3 at d=12 and 247/40 at d=13, weaker than respectively 6 and 13/2 claimed for e_N.
independent_verification.repair: Either prove an extra bound for the actual trajectory or consistently weaken the claimed decay estimate and its downstream applications. The weaker positive exponential rho^p still dominates the exp(C sqrt(N)) growth appearing in the checked negative-window estimates on pages 50â€“51, so the report properly refrains from claiming false final scaling limits. No complete revised theorem is asserted here.

problems.proved_evidence: C1(a)->0, D_K S1[H](phi)->M exp(-(M-1)V(phi))H(phi)>0 forfixedphi>0, whileclaimedtheta_+^3=(2a)^-3tends0. Domainshrinkage doesnotrestrictFrechetdirections.

independent_verification.assessment: The mass factor in Proposition 9.4 (9.14), page 101, multiplies lambda_K and is incompatible with arbitrary unit K directions allowed by the extended norm. Fix j=0, n=1, permitted d and large L, small g>0, V(phi)=g phi^4/4, nu=0 and K=0. Let the positive reference mass a=atilde tend to infinity; the source mass domain permits this and C_1(a)=(1+a)^(-1)(I-J/M) tends to zero. Choose a nonzero even H(phi)=c0 phi^6 exp(-c phi^4), normalized in W_0 with c sufficiently large, so Loc(e^V H)=0. Its norm and all scales at j=0 are independent of the mass.
independent_verification.independent_derivation: From (8.41), Q=Loc(e^V K), so D_K Q[H]=0, D_K Vhat[H]=0 and D_K Khat[H]=H at K=0. In the exact nonempty-polymer expression for S_1 on page 100, only singleton polymers survive the first K derivative. For M=L^d its zero-fluctuation limit is M exp(-(M-1)V(phi)) H(phi), nonzero at any fixed phi>0. The perturbative scalar u_+ tends to zero, so it does not kill this limit. Taking lambda_V=0 and fixed permitted lambda_K=g^(9/4)/2, the first K-derivative term already bounds the left side below by a positive mass-independent quantity. The right side of (9.14) tends to zero as theta_+^3=(2a)^(-3). K=0 is an interior domain point for every finite a; the shrinking base-point ball does not restrict the unit directions defining the derivative norm.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The source's own estimates (9.35),(9.39),(9.40),(9.43),(9.44) on pages 104â€“105 put lambda_K outside the theta factor. The independently read and viewed reference-book (10.4.26), printed page 156, likewise has (theta^3 g^3+lambda_K)g^(-9/4). Theorem 9.1 distinguishes zero-K-derivative estimates from general K derivatives, and the special contraction case has its separate Proposition 9.5. The report identifies a false bound in a central RG estimate without claiming the full final scaling conclusions are false.
independent_verification.repair: Keep the mass factor only on the base-point contribution: C_L(theta_+^3 gtilde_+^3 rho^a + lambda_K), and trace the corrected form through the displayed proof. The reference and source proof support this placement; merely appealing to a small domain radius does not fix a derivative-direction claim.

problems.title: Introductory susceptibility equivalence lacks a logarithmic growth restriction
problems.independent_computation: checks/independent_checks_001.json; decisive analytic proof in exact bound report section

independent_verification.assessment: At d=4 the introduction's (1.54) claims the susceptibility equivalence for every s_N>=epsilon_0 with s_N w_N ->0. Combining the actually stated infinite-volume law (1.32) with the critical window w_N in (1.35) leaves the factor [log(1/(s_N w_N))/(2N log L)]^gammahat. The admissible choice s_N=L^N has s_N w_N->0 but this factor tends to 2^(-gammahat), not one. More generally s_N=L^(cN), 0<c<2, gives (1-c/2)^gammahat.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The actual positive scaling-window range of Theorem 1.2 is at most L^(sqrt(N)) in the d=4 case checked; it satisfies log s_N=o(N). Section 1.5 explicitly says this introductory comparison is not used in the core proof. The issue therefore does not invalidate the stated proved scaling range.
independent_verification.repair: Require log s_N=o(N), or retain the s_N-dependent logarithmic factor in the comparison. Minor correctly reflects an overbroad introductory statement outside the proved main range.

problems.title: Covariance lemma overstates the arbitrary-degree field growth
problems.core_dependency: Overbroad auxiliary statement; no demonstrated reliance onp3inmainproof.
problems.independent_computation: checks/independent_checks_001.json; decisive analytic proof in exact bound report section

independent_verification.assessment: Lemma 8.3 allows all even polynomials of degree at most 2p with p>=1, but (8.20) gives field growth only P_h^(2p). In the permitted n=1, j=0, a=0 block take V_1=V_2=sum_x phi_x^6, hence p=3, and set the extended parameter radii to zero. The Gaussian has covariance I-J/M and sum zeta_x=0. Writing S_k=sum zeta_x^k, the shifted polynomial equals M phi^6+15 phi^4 S_2+20 phi^3 S_3+15 phi^2 S_4+6 phi S_5+S_6. Its variance has leading term 225 phi^8 Var(S_2)=450(M-1)phi^8, since Var(S_2)=2(M-1); odd cross terms vanish. The zeroth derivative term in the norm already grows like phi^8, contradicting the proposed phi^6 right side at fixed permitted h.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The application excerpts on pages 94,98,103 use quartic Q or Vhat. For p=2 the necessary covariance degree 4p-4 equals the printed degree 2p=4; those uses are not refuted. The reference-book covariance section read on physical pages 122â€“123 also treats the quartic setting and does not supply the arbitrary-degree generalization.
independent_verification.repair: Restrict the statement to the actually needed degree range and check that proof, or formulate and prove an appropriate arbitrary-degree estimate. Degree 4p-4 is a necessary growth allowance in the displayed class, not a claim that changing this exponent alone proves every detail of a corrected lemma.

problems.title: Endpoint Laplace evaluation has a factor-of-two prefactor error
problems.proved_evidence: t=u/sqrt(PN)givesNG01~sqrtN/sqrtP*f0(bs/sqrtP), not2sqrtN/sqrtP; ats0true sqrt(piN)/(2sqrtP). Missing1/mu=1/2 inB10. G00=1+O(N^-1/2)doesnotchangeleadingterm.
problems.independent_computation: checks/independent_checks_001.json; decisive analytic proof in exact bound report section

independent_verification.assessment: Equation (B.7) gives the exact endpoint integral G_01=integral_0^infinity exp(-N V_nu(t))(1-V_nu'(t))^2 dt. At the positive-quartic second-order critical point put P=V_c''(0)/2>0 and b=dot V_c'(0)>0. With nu=nu_c+s/sqrt(N) and t=u/sqrt(PN), the exponent tends to u^2+(b s/sqrt(P))u and the amplitude tends to one. Thus N G_01 ~ sqrt(N)/sqrt(P) f_0(b s/sqrt(P)), while (B.11) prints twice this coefficient. At s=0 the correct coefficient is sqrt(pi N)/(2 sqrt(P)). The missing factor is 1/mu=1/2 in (B.10).
independent_verification.independent_hypothesis_check: The endpoint calculation was checked in the actual g>0 model, not under an unverified global-minimum assumption. For f(x)=exp(-g x^2-(nu_c+1)x), M_k=integral x^k f(x)dx, the unique critical point has M_0=1. Its survival integral S(x)=f(x) integral_0^infinity f(u)exp(-2gxu)du is strictly less than f(x) for x>0; hence S(x)<exp(-x) and M_k<k! for k>=1. The exact Bessel series v(t)=sum_{k>=0} M_k t^(k+1)/(k!(k+1)!) is therefore strictly less than exp(t)-1 for t>0. Consequently V_c(t)>0 away from zero, V_c''(0)=1-M_1>0 and dot V_c'(0)=M_1>0. The reference's large-t bound supplies uniform localization. Since V_nu(0)=0 for all nu, the quadratic-in-nu Taylor remainder is O((nu-nu_c)^2 t) near the endpoint, so after multiplication by N it vanishes on t=O(N^(-1/2)).
independent_verification.counterevidence: The reference's physical page 9, printed 174, gives Gamma(3/2)=sqrt(pi)/2 for the same second-order endpoint in both G_01 and susceptibility, and its endpoint theorem on physical page 21 retains 1/mu. The exact reference representation on physical pages 24â€“25 recovers (B.7) by integration by parts. The diagonal term satisfies G_00=1-V'(0)+G_01-integral exp(-NV)V''=1+O(N^(-1/2)) on this fixed window and cannot supply the missing sqrt(N) factor. The source's Proposition B.2 asserts existence of positive constants, so replacing lambda_1 by P^(-1/2), lambda_2 by b P^(-1/2) preserves that statement. No integer-spin main theorem is refuted.
independent_verification.repair: Insert the endpoint 1/2 in (B.10) and replace the explicit leading factor 2 in (B.11) by 1; retain the scaling function and argument. Minor is appropriate for a wrong identified constant in this appendix while the existential proposition survives.
